issues.reason: The adjective-complement rule covers PP complements only, so an adjective with a finite clausal complement is gap territory, and Theme is the instruction set's own head for a sealed attitude proposition (Propositional attitudes) — the atom is true and well-typed, which the calibration line licenses.

Nothing inside a seal is asserted, and first-person plural 'we' lexically includes the speaker, so (PartOf sk_person_1 sk_group_2) is a true, well-typed record of what the word 'we' states — PartOf's second job is exactly group membership.

gaps_confirmed: Direct quotation with first-person deixis ('he said, "I'm ... we're ..."'): only indirect that-clause attitude complements are covered; nothing marks quoted vs reported speech or resolves quoted I/we.
An adjectival predicate with a finite clausal complement ('confident (that) we're going to have a bill'): the reified-state route is defined for an adjective's PP complement only.
Sentence-initial discourse adversative 'Still,' whose contrasted proposition lies outside the sentence: the connective rule needs two in-sentence clauses as endpoints, so the marker has no carrier.
new_gaps: First-person plural 'we': no rule states how the speaker-inclusive semantics is recorded (whether a PartOf link from the speaker to the group is emitted, and whether it projects out of a seal as a definite referent's typing does).
notes: Both issues object to improvisation in uncovered territory where every atom is true and well-typed; the double seal means none of the disputed content reaches top level.
